$comment: Machine-readable surface for /apply-pattern. Human spec: patterns/ai-transparency-disclosure/pattern.md. Expressed AS an invariant cluster (see docs/patterns-registry.md#patterns-as-clusters-of-invariants). The Art. 50 contract pack as a stampable scaffold (chief-wiggum#316) — not just a classification entry in docs/compliance/ai-act.json, but the actual disclosure/provenance/config code /apply-pattern installs.
title: AI Transparency Disclosure
applies_when: the product has a human-facing conversational surface (chat/voice assistant) — Art. 50(1)
the product generates synthetic output (text/image/audio/video) that is persisted or published — Art. 50(2)
the product runs emotion recognition or biometric categorisation, or publishes deepfake media, or publishes AI-generated text on matters of public interest — Art. 50(3)/(4)
NOT when the product has no AI functionality at all — record eu_scope/tier=minimal instead of stamping this pattern
components: first-interaction-disclosure: every human-facing conversational surface mounts a disclosure element reachable AT OR BEFORE the first exchange, never behind a settings/about page

provenance-marker: every synthetic-output write path (text/image/audio/video) persists a machine-readable provenance field alongside the content, not as a separable metadata record that can silently detach

deployer-disclosure-config: emotion-recognition / biometric-categorisation / deepfake-publishing / AI-generated-public-interest-text features carry an explicit disclosure config (on by default), with the human-editorial-responsibility carve-out recorded when claimed, never assumed

protected-disclosure-path: the disclosure component and provenance-marker write path are protected paths (docs/ratchet.md) — a worker cannot quietly remove or feature-flag them off without a human-reviewed goalpost change

invariants.$comment: The cluster this pattern guarantees. Design-derived from Art. 50(1)-(4) and chief-wiggum#316's Decision 4 (check_ai_act.py's 50(1)/50(2)/50(3)(4) checks) — not yet realized in a mined app; this pattern IS the first stamping of it.

cluster.statement: Every human-facing conversational surface has a disclosure element reachable at or before the first interaction (Art. 50(1) has no grace period).
Every synthetic-output write path persists a machine-readable provenance marker alongside the content it produces, never as a detachable side record.

A feature performing emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, or publishing deepfake/AI-generated public-interest content carries an explicit, on-by-default deployer disclosure config; any editorial-responsibility carve-out claimed is recorded with its basis, never assumed silently.
The disclosure component and the provenance-marker write path are protected paths: removing or disabling either is a goalpost change requiring human review, not a worker-diff.

config_dir.description: Where the stamped ai-disclosure.config.json lives (e.g. config/, internal/config).

conversational_surface.description: The primary human-facing chat/voice surface name, for the stamped config's first entry (INV-ATD-001). Add further surfaces to the config by hand after stamping.

synthetic_output_paths.default: TBD: enumerate model-call sites writing persisted/published output
synthetic_output_paths.description: Model-call sites whose output is persisted/published, requiring INV-ATD-002 (provenance marker).

metrics.desc: human-facing AI surfaces with no first-interaction disclosure (target 0)
synthetic-output writes with no provenance marker (target 0)
worker diffs touching the disclosure/provenance protected paths without human review (target 0)
